subject: project:gdl
value: ADDRESSED TO THE INTEGRATOR AND TO THE BF LANE, published early because BF's writes depend on it. The run-29 schema contract names three new optional fields but not WHERE they sit on the record, and the corpus already contains a colliding name. RESOLUTION IMPLEMENTED IN memory_graph/core.py THIS RUN. (1) PLACEMENT. All three additions are TOP-LEVEL record keys: `residual` (object) on attempt records, `falsifier` and `asserted_by` on claim.law records, `held_fixed` on attempt records. This is forced, not stylistic: `attributes.residual` ALREADY EXISTS as a free-prose string in the authoring template ('what remains and why it was left') and is populated as prose across the accepted corpus, so writing the new structured object there would silently overwrite live prose on any record BF touches and would make the type of a single key depend on the record's age. Top-level `residual` also sits beside the existing top-level `residual_class`, which is the field it refines. READERS ARE TOLERANT ANYWAY: every query and gate this run reads top-level first and falls back to `attributes.<field>`, so a record authored either way is found; only the top-level spelling is documented, and only it is written by the template. (2) THE UPDATE PATH FOR BF IS IN-PLACE ADDITIVE ANNOTATION OF ACCEPTED RECORDS, NOT SUPERSESSION. AGENTS.md's 'update facts by superseding, never by deleting' governs changes of FACT; adding `residual`/`falsifier`/`held_fixed` to an existing record changes no fact, it restates in structured form what that record's prose already asserts, and the prose stays verbatim beside it. Superseding instead would be actively harmful three ways, each measurable: it would roughly double the accepted record count for a pure re-encoding; it would push many functions over the 5-attempt-per-function cap and force prune-attempts ejections of live do-not-retry text purely as a side effect of annotation; and it would reset every annotated record's age_days to today, destroying the age-against-the-law-wave screen that claim.RC_stale-reopen-queue-is-a-classifier-artifact.20260901.v1 established as the ONLY sound reopen selector after text-mining was measured to be an artifact. CONDITIONS ON IN-PLACE: purely additive (no existing key's value altered, including valid_from/recorded_at, so ages are preserved); one field-set per record; and `gdlmem validate` plus `gdlmem build` must both stay green after the edit. (3) VALIDATION SPLIT, which is what makes in-place safe. SHAPE validation of the three new fields lives in _validate_record, so it runs on EVERY record at import/validate time and therefore does catch BF's in-place edits: residual must be an object whose signature/family/capability_needed/measured_at are strings-or-null, family must come from the contract's 15-term vocabulary, measured_at must be YYYY-MM-DD, asserted_by must be an array of strings, falsifier and held_fixed must be non-empty strings. It cannot fail on legacy data because no accepted record carries these keys yet, which was verified by grep before shipping. The three REQUIREMENT gates (necessity-language laws require falsifier; postprocessor-class reclassification requires a quoted insns N/N; multi-edit probed_form requires held_fixed) live in stage_record_proposal instead, so they bind NEW proposals only and never retroactively invalidate the ~430 accepted records, exactly as the contract specifies. Net effect for BF: annotate in place, expect shape errors from `gdlmem validate`, and expect no requirement gate to fire on backfill.
